1.explanation: We define a custom ESLint rule (`dump-code-path`) that hooks into the code-path analysis events: `onCodePathStart`, `onCodePathSegmentStart`, `onCodePathSegmentLoop`, and `onCodePathEnd`. During traversal, we gather all code-path segments and their predecessor/successor relationships. At the end of analysis, we print a Graphviz/DOT representation of the control-flow graph. When you run this script (`node reproducible.js`), you will see the dot output for `(null && console.log("b")) ?? console.log("c");`, and you can observe that the edge representing the nullish branch from `a` directly to the `c` evaluation is missing.
1.bug_scenario: When parsing and analyzing the expression `(a && b) ?? c` under ESLint’s code-path analyzer (ECMAScript 2020), the generated control-flow graph is incorrect. In particular, there is no path from the point immediately after evaluating `a` to the evaluation of `c`. In reality, if `a` is `null` or `undefined`, the `&&` short‐circuits and yields that nullish value, which should cause the `??` operator to evaluate `c`. That branch is missing in the dot graph.
